**Derivation.** If $H$ is the foot of the altitude from $A$ to plane $BCD$, then $AB^2=AH^2+HB^2$ and $AC^2=AH^2+HC^2$, so $HB^2-HC^2=S_1^2-S_2^2$; thus $H$ lies on the line through $X$ perpendicular to $BC$ (the locus of points whose squared distances to $B$ and $C$ differ by that constant). Similarly $H$ lies on the perpendicular to $BD$ through $Y$. These two lines are not parallel, so their intersection gives $H$. To construct $X$: if $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$, then $MX=\frac{S_1^2-S_2^2}{2S_4}=\frac{(S_1+S_2)(S_1-S_2)}{2S_4}$, obtainable by a standard fourth-proportional construction; place $X$ on the appropriate side of $M$ according to the sign of $S_1-S_2$. Do the same for $Y$. Finally $AH=\sqrt{S_1^2-BH^2}$, which is the other leg of the right triangle with hypotenuse $S_1$ and leg $BH$.
